brief: Democrats swept the 2026 midterms, flipping seven Senate seats to a 54-44 edge and winning roughly 258 House seats, the party's biggest House majority since 1993, though without a veto-proof Senate majority. Nasdaq futures fell as much as 2.4% overnight on the result before reversing to +0.9% by the New York open, a 929-point round trip Goldman's Rich Privorotsky attributes to pre-election hedges now being monetized rather than fresh conviction, with Nasdaq vol (VXN 30.5) expected to compress as he views AI infrastructure stocks as already oversold. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa will keep the state's data center permitting freeze until broader regulation passes, which Goldman's Mike Cahill says could push gigawatts slated for 2027 into 2028. Data center names IREN, Hut 8 and Applied Digital fell premarket while hyperscalers rose, because Privorotsky argues supply-constrained compute raises the scarcity value of existing capacity even as equipment sellers face an overorder risk. Deutsche's George Saravelos calls the rebound risk positive given reduced Iran escalation odds and Trump's stated openness to compromise, but flags the debt ceiling, binding by Q2 2027, as the next flashpoint. A Republican reconciliation fix before January would remove that uncertainty, while missing the deadline would be dollar negative.
